stem: Your team wants to start testing the new trading feature while the code is still being written. Which of the following can be examined by static testing?
options: Only the trading code, once it compiles without errors
The user stories and acceptance criteria written for the trading feature
Only work products that were written by the test team
Only the trading screen as it behaves in a running build
why: Static testing can examine almost any work product people can read and understand, including user stories and acceptance criteria, long before code exists.

distractorNotes.A: Code can be examined statically even before it compiles, and code is far from the only target.
distractorNotes.C: Anyone's work products can be examined: designers', developers' and managers' as well as testers'.
distractorNotes.D: Watching the running build is dynamic testing: something is executed.

stem: A studio licenses an anti-cheat module that arrives only as an encrypted binary; the contract forbids reverse engineering it. Which work product is NOT appropriate for static testing?
options: The C# scripts the studio wrote to call the anti-cheat module
The design document describing how the anti-cheat module is integrated
The anti-cheat module's encrypted binary itself
The test cases written to check the integration
why: Work products that people cannot sensibly interpret and that must not be analysed by tools (here for legal reasons) are not appropriate for static testing.

distractorNotes.A: The studio's own scripts are readable source code: a classic target for reviews and static analysis.
distractorNotes.B: Design documents are typical review targets.
distractorNotes.D: Testware such as test cases can be reviewed like any other work product.

stem: Which list contains ONLY work products that can be examined by static testing?
options: A test plan, a level-design document, the localisation string table
A test plan, the frame time measured on a device, the localisation string table
The memory use observed during a soak test, a contract, a project schedule
A level-design document, the server's measured response times, a user story
why: Test plans, design documents and string tables are all readable work products, so all three can be reviewed or analysed without running anything.

distractorNotes.B: A frame time measured on a device is the result of executing the game, not a work product to review.
distractorNotes.C: Memory use observed during a soak test comes from running the software: dynamic testing.
distractorNotes.D: Measured response times come from execution; the other two items are fine.

stem: While reviewing the quest design document, a tester notices that two quests both reward the same unique sword. The designer fixes the document in ten minutes. Which benefit of static testing does this BEST illustrate?
options: Static testing shows that the quest document now has no remaining defects
Static testing makes dynamic testing of the quests unnecessary
Static testing measures how efficiently the quest system performs
Defects are found early in the lifecycle, when they are cheaper to fix
why: The defect was found in a document before any code existed, so it was fixed cheaply instead of reaching a build or a release.

distractorNotes.A: Overgeneralisation: testing shows the presence of defects, never their absence.
distractorNotes.B: Static and dynamic testing are complementary; neither replaces the other.
distractorNotes.C: Performance efficiency depends on execution and is measured by dynamic testing.

stem: Which defect can static testing find that dynamic testing typically CANNOT find?
options: A method in the save system that no code path can ever call
A frame-rate drop when 200 enemies spawn at once
A crash that happens only with one specific graphics driver
A memory leak that grows over a three-hour play session
why: Unreachable code is never executed, so no dynamic test can make it fail; a review or a static analyser can see it directly.

distractorNotes.B: A frame-rate drop is a behaviour of the running game, found by dynamic (performance) testing.
distractorNotes.C: A driver-specific crash only shows up when the game runs on that configuration.
distractorNotes.D: A leak that grows over time is typically found by running the game for a long time.

stem: Which statement about the value of static testing is CORRECT?
options: Static testing can only start once the code is complete
Because reviews take effort, static testing always increases the total cost of a project
Reviews help designers, developers and testers reach a shared understanding of the requirements
Static testing is useful only for finding defects in source code
why: Reviewing together makes stakeholders read the same requirement the same way, which prevents misunderstandings from reaching the code.

distractorNotes.A: Static testing can start as soon as any work product exists, e.g. the first draft of the requirements.
distractorNotes.B: Overgeneralisation: reviews cost effort, but finding defects early usually lowers the total project cost.
distractorNotes.D: Requirements, designs and testware are typical static testing targets too.

stem: A tester plays the build and sees the shop charge 100 gold for an item priced at 10. A developer debugs it and finds a wrong constant. The day before, a static analyser had flagged the same constant without running the game. Which statement BEST describes the difference?
options: Static testing found the failure; dynamic testing found the defect
Static testing found the defect directly; dynamic testing caused a failure that then had to be analysed
Both approaches found the same failure, so they are interchangeable
Dynamic testing found the error; static testing found its root cause
why: Static testing works on the work product itself and finds the defect directly; dynamic testing makes the software fail, and the defect behind the failure is found afterwards by analysis (debugging).

distractorNotes.A: Swapped: a failure can only be seen when the software runs, which is dynamic testing.
distractorNotes.C: Static testing found a defect without any failure; the approaches are complementary, not interchangeable.
distractorNotes.D: Term swap: the wrong constant is a defect, not an error, and neither approach found a root cause here.

stem: Which quality characteristic is BEST evaluated by static testing rather than by dynamic testing?
options: How quickly a level loads on the target console
How the matchmaking service behaves with 10,000 players online
How quickly the game reacts to controller input
How maintainable the inventory code is, e.g. its complexity
why: Maintainability does not depend on execution, so it is measured by examining the code itself (static testing).

distractorNotes.A: Load time is performance efficiency, which depends on execution: dynamic testing.
distractorNotes.B: Behaviour under load can only be seen by running the service: dynamic (performance) testing.
distractorNotes.C: Input responsiveness depends on execution on real hardware: dynamic testing.

stem: Which defect is typically EASIER to find with static testing than with dynamic testing?
options: Two requirements in the GDD that contradict each other
A shader that renders incorrectly on one phone model
A desynchronisation that appears only under heavy network load
A save file that becomes corrupt after 50 autosaves
why: Contradictions between requirements live in a document that cannot be executed; reading it (a review) finds them directly.

distractorNotes.B: A device-specific rendering problem shows up when the game runs on that device.
distractorNotes.C: Load-dependent behaviour needs execution under load to appear.
distractorNotes.D: A defect that shows after many autosaves is found by running the game repeatedly.
